checks.name: V1 [the slope of this family IS its integer exponent] the family 1 - (1+Y)^(-n) is differentiated at the origin and its limit at infinity taken, and the slope compared with the exponent
checks.measured: mu_n(Y) = 1 - 1/(Y + 1)**n; slope at origin = n; limit at infinity = 1
checks.reading: the deep-MOND slope equals the exponent exactly, and the function saturates at one for every member. So the slope is not a continuous dial: it is an integer labelling which member of the family you are on, which is a different kind of freedom

checks.name: V2 [and the member with slope two is the one kappa = 1/2 demands] the second member is written out, its slope and saturation confirmed, and the kappa it implies computed from L230's relation
checks.reading: mu = 1 - 1/(1+Y)^2, with no free parameter anywhere in it, has slope exactly two and therefore gives kappa exactly one half. That is the curve L230 asked for

checks.name: V3 [THE TEST: the slope-two member reproduces the framework's kernel inside the relation's own scatter] the acceleration predicted by the candidate is compared with the framework's kernel at sixty points across four decades of baryonic acceleration, and the largest disagreement in dex compared with the observed scatter of the radial acceleration relation
checks.measured: largest |difference| = 0.0264 dex over g_bar/a_0 from 1e-2 to 1e2, against an observed scatter of 0.11 dex and an intrinsic 0.045 dex
checks.reading: the curve that kappa = 1/2 demands is not some exotic shape that galaxies would reject. It tracks the framework's own kernel to within the relation's scatter across the whole measured range

checks.name: V4 [but it is NOT the best-fitting member, and that pulls the other way] the same comparison is run for five members, the closest to the framework's kernel identified, and its root-mean-square difference compared with the slope-two member's
checks.measured: root-mean-square difference by member: {r[0]: round(r[3], 4) for r in rows}; best is n = 1 at 0.0107 dex, against n = 2 at 0.0154 dex -- better by 1.44x
checks.reading: the member that best reproduces the framework's own kernel is n = 1, not the n = 2 that kappa selects. So the rotation curves lean the OTHER way, toward kappa = 1, which the kappa measurements exclude at seven sigma. Both members sit inside the relation's scatter, so neither is ruled out by it -- but the honest statement is that this test does not support n = 2 over n = 1, it merely fails to exclude it. An earlier draft of this lane asserted the opposite and was wrong

checks.name: V5 [the relation's scatter admits more than one member, so this is a consistency check and not a measurement of the slope] the members lying inside the observed and the intrinsic scatter are counted separately
checks.measured: inside the observed scatter (0.11 dex): n = [1, 2, 3, 4, 8]; inside the intrinsic (0.045 dex): n = [1, 2, 3]
checks.reading: several members survive the observed scatter, so rotation curves alone do not measure the slope. What they do is confirm that the member kappa selects is allowed -- which was not guaranteed, since a curve rising twice as fast at the origin could easily have been excluded outright

checks.name: V6 [an integer exponent is weaker freedom than a continuous coefficient, but it is still freedom] the kind of choice remaining is stated and compared with the continuous parameter L230 ruled out
checks.measured: L230 forbade inserting a factor of two because a factor of two is a continuous free parameter. Choosing n = 2 from {1, 2, 3, ...} is a discrete choice, which is weaker, but it is NOT a derivation: nothing in this lane says why the exponent is two
checks.reading: so the honest status is that the curve EXISTS, is parameter-free once the integer is named, gives kappa = 1/2 exactly, and fits the rotation curves. What is missing is a reason for the integer, and that is now the whole of the remaining gap

checks.name: V7 [the gap, sized] the remaining unknown is stated as a choice among a countable set rather than a continuum, and the size of that set compared with the continuum L226 started from
checks.measured: the remaining freedom is one integer; L226 began with a free FUNCTION, L229 reduced it to two continuous numbers, L230 to one, and this lane to a choice among {'n = 2 selected by kappa': 2, 'n = 1, the simple function': 1, 'n -> infinity, exponential': 8}
checks.reading: a free function, then two numbers, then one number, then one integer. Each step was a real reduction and none of them was a derivation. The last step is the smallest and it is still open

checks.name: V8 [the verdict on the swing] whether the curve was found is stated plainly against what was asked, including what the fit does and does not support
checks.measured: ASKED: a parameter-free curve saturating at one with slope two. FOUND: mu(Y) = 1 - 1/(1+Y)^2 -- slope exactly two, saturates at one, no free coefficient, kappa = 1/2 exactly, and within 0.026 dex of the framework's kernel across four decades. NOT FOUND: a reason for the exponent. NOT SUPPORTED: preference over n = 1, which fits the kernel 1.44x better and implies the excluded kappa = 1
checks.reading: the curve exists and is allowed. It is not selected by the rotation curves, and no reason for its exponent is given here. Calling it derived would be wrong on both counts
